prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures a transition from an open doorway looking outdoors in frames 1–2—where the camera wearer stands within arm's reach (~0.3–1.0 m) above a table saw in front of them, flanked by open wooden door leaves to the left and right—to an indoor workshop in frames 3–5 as the wearer turns ~180 degrees and steps inward. In frames 1–2, the wearer's extended right arm and a thin wooden strip held in their hand appear brightest (~0.3–0.8 m), the table saw sits at ~0.7–1.3 m below and in front of the viewpoint, and the outdoor ground slopes away into dark background (>3 m). As the wearer turns into the room in frames 3–5, the right-side doorframe passes very close on the right (~0.3–0.6 m) while the interior layout emerges: a wooden bench structure and a crouched coworker on the left (~1.8–3.0 m away, moving closer to ~1.5–2.2 m by frame 5), a vertical stack of white boards in the upper-middle background (~2.5–3.5 m, ~1.5 m behind the coworker), a yellow miter saw on the floor to the lower right (~1.5–2.0 m), and a blue chair further back to the right (~3.5–4.5 m, ~1.5 m right of the board stack). The coworker bends forward facing downward toward the wooden structure on the left, keeping the wooden panels within their arm's reach while looking away from the camera wearer, and is partially occluded at the frame edges in frame 5. The depth map makes the continuous 3D floor gradient, the vertical relief of the leaning board stack, and the relative distance gap between the foreground door jamb and mid-ground objects much easier to judge than in the dark, high-contrast RGB frames, though it is unreliable on thin floor cables, fine wood scraps, and the dark indoor shadow of frame 3 where the coworker and bench blend into mid-grey.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a sparse subset of foreground and mid-ground entities—specifically `person` masks and a single `chair` mask—while omitting the doorway, table saw, wooden boards, miter saw, and floor layout entirely. In frames 1–3, a pink `person` mask at the bottom edge marks the camera wearer's own lower torso, feet, and extended right arm (~0.2–0.7 m below and in front of the camera, within immediate arm's reach of the unsegmented table saw in frames 1–2 and partially cropped by the bottom frame boundary), documenting the wearer's arm extending forward in frame 2 and retracting as they turn indoors in frame 3. In frames 4–5, a `person` mask identifies the crouched coworker to the left of center at roughly 1.5–2.5 m distance, bending forward and facing downward toward the left (not looking toward the camera wearer), as their relative position shifts downward and leftward into closer range (~1.5 m) as the wearer approaches. In frame 4 only, a purple `chair` mask detects the blue folding chair in the upper-right background (~3.5–4.0 m from the wearer, ~2.0 m to the right of the coworker and just right of the occluding board stack). While this map cleanly separates the wearer's self-body silhouette and the coworker's bent contour from cluttered workshop backgrounds that are visually busy in RGB, it is highly unreliable across the strip: it misses the coworker and background chair completely in frame 3, drops the camera wearer's visible right foot at the bottom of frames 4–5, loses the chair in frame 5, and fails to segment any tools, lumber, or structural surfaces.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost completely blank across all five frames, detecting only a single magenta right-hand skeleton for the camera wearer in the lower-left quadrant of frame 1. In frame 1, this hand skeleton lies ~0.4–0.5 m below and slightly left of center in front of the camera wearer, gripping the thin wooden strip within arm's reach just above the table saw (~0.8 m away), with the fingers curled inward and oriented forward and slightly left. The map provides no spatial data on the scene layout, the doorway, the workshop furniture, or distances between objects, nor does it track the camera wearer's right hand as it pushes the wood forward over the saw in frame 2 and retracts in frame 3. Furthermore, it completely fails to detect the body or hands of the crouched coworker located ~1.5–3.0 m away on the left in frames 3–5, offering no indication from the map alone that the coworker is bent over facing the wooden structure, looking away from the camera wearer, and reaching toward the panels in front of them. Although the single hand skeleton in frame 1 clarifies the exact articulated finger and wrist configuration holding the wooden strip against the sunlit floor better than RGB alone, the pose map is severely unreliable due to extreme egocentric foreshortening, top-down viewing angles, self-occlusion of the coworker's hunched body, and motion blur across frames 2–5.
